arabian-desert.bounds_prose: Wikipedia's infobox says the desert 'occupies almost the entire Arabian Peninsula with an area of 2,330,000 square kilometers (900,000 sq mi).' The intro states it 'stretches from Yemen to the Persian Gulf and Oman to Jordan and Iraq.' Named subdivisions: Rub' al-Khali (Empty Quarter, south), Ad-Dahna (corridor linking north and south), An-Nafud (north Saudi Arabia, 65,000 km2), Sharqiya/Wahiba Sands (Oman east coast, isolated sand sea), Tuwaiq escarpment (800 km limestone arc), Umm al Samim quicksand flats.
arabian-desert.north_limit: Jordan and Iraq (article gives no explicit line; An-Nafud sits in northern Saudi Arabia, roughly the Jordan/Iraq/Kuwait border zone, ~29-32N)
arabian-desert.south_limit: Yemen (Rub' al-Khali's southern edge and Yemen border, ~12-13N)
arabian-desert.west_limit: Article's infobox lists Egypt (Sinai) as one of the desert's countries, implying the western edge reaches the Red Sea/Suez area (~32-34E); article does not name the Asir/Hejaz mountains as a western boundary
arabian-desert.east_limit: Persian Gulf and Oman (Sharqiya/Wahiba Sands on Oman's east coast, ~58-60E)
arabian-desert.notes: The article never mentions the Asir, Hejaz, Yemeni highlands, or Hajar (Oman) mountains by name, and gives no statement on whether they are included or excluded from the desert. Because the infobox lists Yemen, Oman, and Egypt (Sinai) as countries the desert occupies, and the area figure (2,330,000 km2) is close to the full Arabian Peninsula's ~3,000,000 km2, the Wikipedia definition appears to treat the desert as covering nearly the whole peninsula including its mountainous margins, rather than excluding the Asir/Hejaz/Yemen highlands or Hajar range the way some other sources do. Treat mountain-range exclusion as UNCONFIRMED by this article. Lat/lon bounding box derived from: south = Yemen border/Rub' al-Khali (~12N); north = Jordan/Iraq/Kuwait zone where An-Nafud sits (~29-32N, used 32N as outer bound); west = Sinai/Suez area implied by 'Egypt (Sinai)' in country list (~32.3E); east = Oman's Sharqiya Sands on the east coast (~59-60E).

kyzylkum-desert.bounds_prose: Article: 'It covers about 298,000 km2 (115,000 sq mi)' and lies 'in the land between the confluent rivers Amu Darya and Syr Darya.' 'Today it is divided among Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan,' and 'is mainly located in Uzbekistan.' Terrain is 'mainly an extensive plain at an altitude up to 300 m above sea level, with a number of depressions and highlands (Sultanuizdag, Bukantau).' Kerki, on the Amu Darya, is cited as being on the desert's margin.
kyzylkum-desert.north_limit: Toward the Aral Sea / lower Syr Darya (Kazakhstan), ~45N
kyzylkum-desert.south_limit: The Amu Darya valley near the Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan border (near Kerki), ~38N
kyzylkum-desert.east_limit: Toward the Syr Darya / Tashkent region, ~67-68E
kyzylkum-desert.notes: Article gives no explicit numeric boundary coordinates; the box is derived from the two bounding rivers it names (Amu Darya on the southwest, Syr Darya on the northeast) and the Aral Sea, which the Kyzylkum abuts to the north. Internal highlands (Sultanuizdag, Bukantau) are described as within the desert, not excluded from it.

sinai-peninsula.bounds_prose: 'Its northern shore lying on the southern Mediterranean Sea' and 'its southwest and southeast shores on the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba of the Red Sea.' 'It is linked to the African continent by the Isthmus of Suez, 125 kilometres... wide... containing the Suez Canal.' The Egypt-Israel border 'runs in an almost straight line from Rafah on the Mediterranean shore to Taba on the Gulf of Aqaba.' 'The southernmost tip is the Ras Muhammad National Park.' Land area 'about 60,000 km2 (23,000 sq mi).'
sinai-peninsula.north_limit: Mediterranean Sea coast, near Rafah/El Arish, ~31.3N
sinai-peninsula.west_limit: Suez Canal / Gulf of Suez (Isthmus of Suez), ~32.3-32.6E
sinai-peninsula.east_limit: Gulf of Aqaba and the Rafah-Taba border line with Israel, ~34.9E
sinai-peninsula.notes: Bounding box derived from named places: Suez (west, ~32.55E), Rafah on the Mediterranean (north border point, ~34.25E, ~31.29N) and Taba on the Gulf of Aqaba (east border point, ~34.9E, ~29.49N), and Ras Muhammad as the southern apex (~27.7N). Peninsula is entirely within Egypt; it borders Israel/Gaza to the northeast but that border is the peninsula's eastern edge, not part of it.

delmarva-peninsula.bounds_prose: 'Occupied by the majority of the state of Delaware and parts of the Eastern Shore of Maryland and Eastern Shore of Virginia,' 'bordered by the Chesapeake Bay on the west, Pocomoke Sound on the southwest, and the Delaware River, Delaware Bay, and the Atlantic Ocean on the east.' 'The peninsula is 170 miles (274 km) long,' ranging '70 miles (113 km) near its center, to 12 miles (19 km) at the isthmus on its northern edge.' The 'northern isthmus... is transected by the sea-level Chesapeake and Delaware Canal,' with the Atlantic Seaboard Fall Line passing through Newark and Wilmington, Delaware, and Elkton, Maryland. 'Cape Charles forms the southern tip of the peninsula in Virginia.' 'Total land area south of the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal is 5,454 sq mi (14,130 km2).'
delmarva-peninsula.north_limit: The C&D Canal isthmus (~39.55-39.6N), with Delaware's political extent up to the Pennsylvania border a bit further north (~39.8N)
delmarva-peninsula.notes: The 14,130 km2 figure is explicitly only the land area SOUTH of the C&D Canal; the full peninsula (including the narrow isthmus up to the Pennsylvania line) is somewhat larger. Lat/lon box derived from Cape Charles (south tip, ~37.1N), the C&D Canal/Pennsylvania border area (north, ~39.6-39.8N), the Chesapeake Bay's western shoreline of the Eastern Shore (west, ~76.3W near indentations like Tilghman Island), and the Atlantic barrier-island coast near Ocean City/Cape Henlopen (east, ~75.0W).

peloponnese.bounds_prose: '21,549.6 square kilometres (8,320.3 mi2) in area, and constitutes the southernmost part of mainland Greece.' 'It is connected to the mainland by the Isthmus of Corinth, where the Corinth Canal was constructed in 1893.' The article names the Gulf of Corinth (separated from the Saronic Gulf by the isthmus) and the 'Messenian Gulf, Laconian Gulf, and Argolic Gulf' framing its four southern promontories: Messenian, Mani, Cape Malea, and Argolid.
peloponnese.north_limit: Isthmus of Corinth / Gulf of Corinth, ~38.0-38.4N
peloponnese.south_limit: Cape Tainaron / Cape Malea (southern tips of the Mani and Malea promontories), ~36.4N
peloponnese.west_limit: Ionian Sea coast (western Peloponnese, e.g. Pylos/Kyparissia area), ~21.1E
peloponnese.east_limit: Argolic Gulf / Cape Malea (Myrtoan Sea side), ~23.2E
peloponnese.notes: Article does not explicitly say the Corinth Canal makes the Peloponnese a true island; it continues to describe it as a peninsula connected via the Isthmus of Corinth (with the Rio-Antirrio bridge and canal-crossing bridges as modern links). Bounding box derived from the Isthmus of Corinth/Gulf of Corinth in the north, and the four named south-pointing capes (Messenian, Mani/Tainaron, Malea, Argolid) as the southern, western, and eastern extremes.

indo-gangetic-plain.bounds_prose: '700,000 km2 (270,000 sq mi) across the northern and north-eastern part of South Asia. It encompasses northern and eastern India, eastern Pakistan, southern Nepal, and almost all of Bangladesh.' 'It stretches from the Himalayas in the north to the northern edge of the Deccan Plateau in the south' and '...to the Vindhyas and Satpura and the Chota Nagpur Plateau in the south.' Intro also says it extends 'from North East India in the east to the Iranian border in the west,' but detailed sections instead describe 'The Sindh Plains forms the western part of the plains... to the west of the Thar Desert' (Pakistan) as the actual western portion, and 'The Brahmaputra Valley largely covers... Assam' plus the 'Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta... Bangladesh and... West Bengal' as the eastern portion. Formed by deposits of the Indus, Ganges, and Brahmaputra rivers.
indo-gangetic-plain.north_limit: The Himalayas (foothill line, varies ~28-34N along its length)
indo-gangetic-plain.south_limit: Vindhya/Satpura ranges and Chota Nagpur Plateau edge, ~21-24N
indo-gangetic-plain.west_limit: Sindh Plains west of the Thar Desert, Pakistan (article's intro loosely says 'Iranian border' but its own regional detail points to the Sindh/Thar area, ~66-68E, well east of Iran at ~61E)
indo-gangetic-plain.east_limit: Brahmaputra Valley (Assam) and the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta into Bangladesh/West Bengal, ~92-96E
indo-gangetic-plain.notes: There is an internal inconsistency in the article: its opening sentence says the plain reaches 'the Iranian border' in the west, but its regional breakdown only goes as far west as the Sindh Plains/Thar Desert region of Pakistan (roughly 66-68E), far short of the actual Iran border (~61E). I used the more specific Sindh/Thar description for the western edge of the bounding box rather than the literal 'Iranian border' claim, and flag this discrepancy. Eastern edge extended out to include the Assam/Brahmaputra valley and the Bangladesh delta, per the article's own text, even though the plain is popularly associated mainly with the Ganges basin.

campos.bounds_prose: English Wikipedia has no standalone article for 'Campos Sulinos'; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campos_Sulinos redirects to the 'Pampas' article, which treats the Brazilian portion only briefly: 'all of Uruguay; and Brazil's southernmost state, Rio Grande do Sul' and 'the interior areas (mainly in the southern part of the Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul and Uruguay) have low ranges of hills,' bordering 'the Atlantic Forest and the Great Chaco Plain' to the north; no Brazil-specific area figure, only the combined Pampas figure of >1,200,000 km2 across Argentina/Brazil/Uruguay. The WWF ecoregion covering this same area, 'Uruguayan Savanna' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguayan_Savanna), gives more specific figures: area '353,573 km2'; 'bounded on the east by the South Atlantic Ocean'; 'bounded on the south by the Rio de la Plata estuary'; 'The Uruguay River forms the western boundary'; to the north 'it transitions to the Alto Parana Atlantic forests and Araucaria moist forests' in southern Brazil. Spans Uruguay, Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil), and parts of Argentina along the Uruguay River.
campos.north_limit: Transition to Araucaria moist forests / Atlantic Forest in southern Rio Grande do Sul (article gives no exact line; roughly the RS/Santa Catarina climatic transition, ~28-29S)
campos.east_limit: South Atlantic coast of Rio Grande do Sul/Uruguay (e.g. Torres, RS), ~49.7W
campos.notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: the area_km2 (353,573) and the lat/lon box are for the ENTIRE Uruguayan Savanna/Campos ecoregion (Uruguay + Rio Grande do Sul + a strip of Argentina along the Uruguay River), because neither English Wikipedia article gives a Rio Grande-do-Sul-only figure. This IS confirmed to be the Campos Sulinos of southern Brazil (grasslands of Rio Grande do Sul, part of the Pampa biome), NOT Campos dos Goytacazes (a city/lowland in Rio de Janeiro state) and NOT the Campos Sertao/Cerrado of northeast Brazil - those are unrelated features not discussed in either source article. Secondary source used (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campos_Sulinos redirects to Pampas) because the Pampas article's Brazil-specific content is thin; the Uruguayan Savanna ecoregion article was used as it directly matches the same grasslands with an explicit area figure and boundary description. Lat/lon box derived from: south = Rio de la Plata estuary (~34.6-35S); west = Uruguay River (~58W near Salto); east = Atlantic coast of Rio Grande do Sul near Torres (~49.7W); north = qualitative transition to Araucaria/Atlantic Forest in southern RS, no exact coordinate given so estimated at the RS/Santa Catarina border latitude (~28-29S).

veld.bounds_prose: 'Veld is a type of wide-open, rural landscape in Southern Africa. Particularly, it is a flat area covered in grass or low scrub, especially in the countries of South Africa, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, Zimbabwe, and Botswana.' 'Much of the interior of Southern Africa consists of a high plateau, the higher portions 1,500-2,100 m (4,900-6,900 ft) of which are known as the highveld.' 'These higher, cooler areas (generally more than 1,500 m or 4,900 ft above sea level) are characterised by flat or gently undulating terrain, vast grasslands.' 'The lowlands, below about 500 m (1,640 ft) altitude, along South Africa's northern border with Botswana and Zimbabwe... is known as the lowveld,' which is 'generally hotter and less intensely cultivated than the highveld.'
veld.north_limit: Extends into Zimbabwe and Botswana (lowveld along South Africa's northern border with those countries)
veld.south_limit: Southern edge of the interior plateau in South Africa's interior (Free State/Eastern Cape interior)
veld.west_limit: Into Namibia/Botswana (western part of the veld belt, more arid)
veld.east_limit: Escarpment down to the Lowveld of Mpumalanga/Eswatini/southern Mozambique border area
veld.notes: 'Veld' as used by the article is a broad umbrella term covering the whole grassy interior-plateau landscape (Highveld + Middleveld + Lowveld + Bushveld), not just the Highveld specifically; the article gives no total area figure so area_km2 is null. Elevation subdivisions given: Highveld >1,500 m (the core high interior plateau, mainly Free State/Gauteng/Mpumalanga highlands and Lesotho's fringes), Lowveld <500 m (along South Africa's northern border with Botswana/Zimbabwe, extending into the Kruger/Eswatini/southern Mozambique lowlands). Because the article names six countries (South Africa, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, Zimbabwe, Botswana) without giving exact coordinates, the lat/lon box is a rough estimate spanning the interior plateau of Southern Africa from roughly southern Namibia/Northern Cape in the west to the Mpumalanga/Eswatini escarpment in the east, and from the Eastern Cape interior in the south to the Zimbabwe/Botswana border area in the north; treat this bounding box as considerably less precise than the others since the source article supplies no named boundary lines or coordinates.
